fields.description:
## Problem
The .bridge_state/projects.json write path VIOLATES the project invariant that every
tickets-branch mutation must (1) run under the unified store write lock AND (2)
auto-commit + auto-publish. projects_store.set_project/remove_project ->
projects_store._write_record is a bare tempfile+os.replace: no lock, no commit, no push.
It also (a) hand-rolls atomic write instead of the shared rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write
seam, and (b) accepts any project key with no _validate_project_key guard. This forced the
ad-hoc hand-commits behind incident 05b8-4efe-8d58-4c27 (LEG/ONE/TWO/ZERO leak).

## Use the EXISTING seams (NO new facade, NO redesign)
Both required seams already exist and are the standard path:
- rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write — the shared crash-atomic file write (umask/perms/fsync).
- rebar._store.push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch(tracker, *, message=...) — "Commit all
  pending tracker changes UNDER ITS WRITE LOCK, then push." It already composes
  _lock.write_lock(dual_window=True, retries=write_path_retries) + check_no_rebase_in_progress
  (rebase guard) + git add + commit + push_tickets_branch. It is the public seam (also
  `python -m rebar._store.push commit-and-push`). This is exactly the two-part invariant.

## Approach (minimal reuse)
1. projects_store._write_record: swap the hand-rolled mkstemp/os.replace for
   fsutil.atomic_write. Prove the on-disk bytes are byte-identical (json.dump indent=2,
   sort_keys=True + trailing "\n").
2. After a mapping mutation, publish it through the EXISTING seam: call
   push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch(tracker, message="bridge: update projects mapping")
   so set_project/remove_project are durable + published under the write lock with no
   ad-hoc git. (Wire at the mutation entry point — projects_store mutators or their
   lib/CLI callers in _lib_ops; keep the read path untouched.)
3. Add write-time key validation: set_project rejects a syntactically-invalid key via the
   existing fetcher._validate_project_key (import/reuse it; do not duplicate the regex).
4. Codify the two-part invariant in docs/concurrency.md ("Mutating the tracker" section):
   EVERY tickets-branch mutation runs under write_lock AND auto-commits+publishes.

## Constraints
- BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING atomic-write swap (pin exact serialized bytes with a RED test).
- Preserve load_mapping's ABSENT=legal-empty / MALFORMED=fail-closed semantics unchanged.
- Do NOT touch resolve_project / legacy_default semantics (that is ticket a011).
- Do NOT add any new commit/push/lock helper — reuse commit_and_push_tickets_branch as-is.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A projects.json mutation is committed to the tickets branch and pushed under the write
   lock via commit_and_push_tickets_branch — no ad-hoc git, no new seam.
2. projects_store uses fsutil.atomic_write; serialized bytes unchanged (pinned test).
3. set_project rejects a syntactically-invalid key ("le-g", "", "1x") non-zero, no write.
4. docs/concurrency.md states the two-part invariant.

## Test plan
- RED unit pinning projects.json serialized bytes across the atomic_write swap.
- RED unit: set_project("le-g", ...) exits/raises non-zero, no file written.
- Unit asserting a mapping mutation calls push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch (patch the
  seam; assert invoked with the tracker) — the invariant regression guard.

## Sequencing
Edits projects_store.py + docs/concurrency.md (+ tests); reuses push/fsutil (no edit).
Disjoint from A (fetcher.py), C (fetcher.py), D (access_check/__main__). Ticket E adopts
the SAME existing seam for the parity siblings and is sequenced after this one only so the
two do not both edit the reconciler commit path concurrently.
